newsitem.title: USA: Clintons snorkel in turquoise waters off St. John.
newsitem.headline: Clintons snorkel in turquoise waters off St. John.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton and his family donned snorkels and fins on Friday and took in some undersea sights around the Virgin Islands.
On a day of blue skies and calm seas, the Clintons boarded a 53-foot catamaran, called Lady Lynsey, for a four-hour sail of Caribbean waters near the U.S. Virgin Islands of St. Thomas and St. John.

They dropped anchor near Lovango Cay, a tiny spot on the map near St. John. There, they put on their snorkeling gear and wetsuits, and spent about two hours looking at the sights available, such as parrotfish, trumpetfish or sea turtles. A guide accompanied them.
"They saw lots of fishies," said a White House spokeswoman, Mary Ellen Glynn, who added that Clinton found the outing "fascinating."
Now uninhabited, Lovango is known to the locals as a place where brothels were located at the turn of the century at a time when the larger islands were quite religious.
"Fishermen used to go over there," said Dennis Roderick, captain of the charter boat Limnos II, which carried the press pool that accompanied the Clintons' boat on part of its tour.
He said the island was nicknamed "Love-and-Go," which was eventually shortened to Lovango.

It was the first outing taken by the Clintons since they arrived on Wednesday night for their Caribbean vacation. In keeping with the Clintons' aim for a private vacation, reporters and photographers have been kept far away from them and the Sand Dollar villa on St. Thomas where they are staying.

After the snorkeling, their blue-and-white vessel sailed back over the calm, sparkling turquoise waters of Pillsbury Sound -- a collapsed volcano -- to St. Thomas, where Clinton played golf at Mahogany Run Golf Course.
The Clintons return to Washington on Sunday.
